The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), further exempts William C. Shambaugh from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending August 31, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. The recital names the earlier exemption Executive Order No. 8096 of April 21, 1939; those are earlier instruments, not events on this order. First end: the order's own stated end, August 31, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending August 31, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of August 31, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when August 31, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held.

Shambaugh remain in service past the retirement age that would otherwise have required automatic separation; service rendered while the exemption ran is an accrued effect that remains after the stated end date.
